chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ahmad ibn Amr ibn Sa'id, from Wardan, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever is from Mecca at a travel distance of ten miles cannot enter it except in Ihram.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٍ: Ihram, the state of ritual consecration
key_terms.مَسِيرَةِ عَشَرَةِ أَمْيَالٍ: a travel distance of ten miles

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for entering Mecca if one lives within ten miles?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the Miqat (boundary of consecration) for residents of Mecca, establishing a ten-mile radius as the threshold for entering the Haram in a state of Ihram. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the sanctity of the sacred precincts, distinguishing between casual entry and ritual entry, and serves as a foundational precedent for the geographical limits of the Haram's legal status.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Ahmad Bin Amro Bin Saeed, from Wardaan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> having said:
‘The one who was away from Makkah upon a travel distance of ten miles cannot enter it (the Harram) except in Ihraam’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from Ahmad ibn ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Wardan who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Whoever lives at a distance of ten miles from Makkah must not enter Makkah without Hiram.’”
